question: Can a class-balanced LightGBM model with cross-validated tuning, averaged over several few-shot episodes, beat a neural-network stand-in for the paper's residual-SE few-shot detector on a public sensor-based activity dataset with only 10 labelled examples per class?
method: UCI HAR (OpenML 1478) as stand-in for road-alert sensor signals. 5 episodes of 10-shot-per-class training sampling from a stratified 70% pool; evaluation on the held-out 30% test split. Baseline: MLPClassifier on standardized features. Improved: class-balanced LightGBM with 3-fold stratified CV grid search inside each few-shot set. Metric: macro-F1 on the test split.
baseline: MLPClassifier (256 hidden units, standardized inputs), stand-in for residual-SE network
improved: Class-balanced LightGBM; num_leaves, n_estimators and min_child_samples chosen by 3-fold stratified CV on the few-shot training set only
notes: OpenML 1478 is distributed as one combined table, so the official UCI train/test split is not recoverable; a single stratified 70/30 split (seed 42) is used instead. This is a stand-in dataset, not the paper's road-alert signals, and the MLP is a generic stand-in, not a reproduction of the residual-SE network. Results come from 5 episodes only, so differences may be within noise; std is over episodes.
